# @hazelnut/core

> Hazelnut — a Deno backend framework where one `defineResource` is the single
> source for the type faces, HTTP routes, Postgres schema, MCP tools, and the op-pipeline.
> Everything derives at boot by composition; nothing is generated to disk. Apache-2.0.

This index describes `@hazelnut/core@0.44.0`. What changed in each version — Breaking, Added, Fixed,
and the handbook pages it touched — is the GitHub Release for its tag:
https://github.com/Hazelnut-17/hazelnut/releases/tag/v0.44.0

Types are always inferred (`z.infer` / Drizzle), never code-generated, so there is no watcher and
nothing to keep in sync. No business concepts live in the core — multi-tenancy is a recipe over the
generic `scope` primitive.

Stack: Deno 2.x · Hono · Zod 4 · Drizzle + drizzle-kit · PostgreSQL 16+ (schema-per-module) ·
Deno.cron + a Postgres transactional outbox · Result · Deno.test + fast-check.

```sh
deno run --allow-read --allow-write=. --allow-env --allow-run=deno,deno.exe,git --allow-net jsr:@hazelnut/core/cli new my-app
```

## The surface loads in rungs — pay per rung

You do not need the whole vocabulary to ship. Each rung is a working app and names its cost up front.

**Rung 1 — a CRUD backend plus one guarded operation (11 concepts).** Exactly what the scaffolded app imports, and
no more: `createApp`, `defineConfig`, `defineResource`, `applySchema`, `pgliteDb`, `postgresDb`, `defineOp`, `requires`, `ok`, `OpDecl`, `Ctx` from `hazelnut`. `defineResource` is the one that pays — one per entity, deriving the type
faces, HTTP routes, Postgres schema, MCP tools and the op-pipeline. The guarded operation is on both
doors, while the row rule stays the ownership shorthand. Around them sit three things that are shape
rather than vocabulary — the
`app.ts` (pure model) / `main.ts` (served boot) split, the `hazelnut migrate` loop, and per-resource
`features: {}` toggles. Read `docs/rundown.md` sections 2-5.

**Rung 2 — a named boundary, domain errors, and identity (+8 concepts).**
`defineModule`, `err`, `Result`, `defineAuth`, `derivePerms`, `userActor`, `can` from `hazelnut`; `all` from `hazelnut/query`. With them come a module boundary, a `scope` resolver, and the claim question a real app must
answer. Deny-by-default is enforced at build, so the route and row posture stay written decisions.
Read `docs/rundown.md` sections 6-7 in order — it is the single end-to-end walkthrough of exactly
this rung.

**Rung 3 — one verb per concern (+1 each).** Pull one in only when its concern is real; nothing here is
needed to ship rung 1 or 2:

| verb | import from | reach for it when you want |
|---|---|---|
| `defineJob` | `hazelnut/async` | Work on a schedule |
| `definePerms` | `hazelnut` | A perm key no resource seeds |
| `definePrompt` | `hazelnut/faces` | A reusable prompt over MCP |
| `defineReadModel` | `hazelnut/async` | A maintained read projection |
| `defineSubscriber` | `hazelnut/async` | React to an event |
| `defineTask` | `hazelnut/async` | Long work a caller polls |
| `defineUpcaster` | `hazelnut/async` | Read an older stored event |
| `defineVersion` | `hazelnut` | Breaking API shape change |
| `defineView` | `hazelnut` | A narrowed / cross-module read |
| `defineWebhook` | `hazelnut/async` | Call OUT to a third party |
| `defineWorker` | `hazelnut/async` | A durable work queue |
| `defineWorkflow` | `hazelnut/async` | Multi-step durable process |

**What it costs, honestly.** Summed, the vocabulary is roughly two dozen concepts — but no task loads
them all, and there is no hidden fourth rung. The abstraction pays off past ~10 resources with authz,
audit, events and an MCP/OpenAPI surface; below that a hand-written CRUD service is less machinery.

## What one resource can declare

These are the guarantees a `defineResource` turns on — the whole vocabulary, so nothing here needs a
page open to know it exists. Each is opt-in and each derives its own schema, faces and invariants.

| declare | what it adds |
|---|---|
| `timestamps` | `created_at` / `updated_at` — stored columns; they reach a response only if you name them in a read route's `columns` (§2) |
| `scope` | row-scoping: a scope-key column, stamped on write and conjoined on read |
| `softDelete` | `deleted_at`; delete becomes soft, and reads exclude deleted rows |
| `audit` (+ `onRow`) | an audit trail per mutation, masking the `sensitive` and `encrypted` fields. Declaring it REQUIRES declaring `sensitive` — `sensitive: []` is the "no PII here" answer, and nothing else masks the diff. `audit: { fields, snapshot }` records only those columns, and `snapshot: true` also stores the masked before/after row |
| `sequence` | a per-resource minted counter column, such as `invoiceNo` |
| `expiry` | `expires_at` and read exclusion; an asynchronous purge unless you set `purge: false`; with `purge: false` a read-model sink over it resyncs hourly (`<source>:readmodel-resync`), so the scheduler must run |
| `temporal` | `valid_from` / `valid_to` effective-dating plus `asOf` reads (`find` / `findOrFail` / `exists` / `search` take `{ asOf? }`); `{ noOverlap: [cols] }` adds a GiST EXCLUDE over those keys — partial on `deleted_at IS NULL` when softDelete or rectifiable hides non-live rows; a read-model sink over it resyncs hourly (`<source>:readmodel-resync`), so the scheduler must run |
| `versioning` | an optimistic-lock `version`. `update`, `delete` and a `tree` resource's `move` all require the version you read — `findForUpdate(id)` locks the row and hands it to you; over HTTP, send `If-Match` on the PATCH and the DELETE |
| `immutable` | append-only, whole-resource or field-level set-once; `{ tamperEvident: true }` adds an HMAC-SHA-256 hash chain; `{ rectifiable: true }` adds `ctx.data.<r>.rectify` (GDPR Art. 16) — a correction append that stamps `deleted_at` on the superseded head so default reads hide it |
| `singleton` | exactly one row, per scope or per app. A versioned singleton's `ctx.config.<name>.replace(patch, row.version)` requires the value from `getOrSeedConfig()`; a stale token is a `conflict`, not a blind full-row write. |
| `tree` | a self-referential hierarchy (`parent_id`); re-parent with `move(id, parentId)`, which also takes the version you read, `move(id, parentId, row.version)`, when the resource is versioned; `create`, `update` and `move` need a live, in-scope parent (a foreign, soft-deleted, or superseded one is `notFound`), `depth` counts only ancestors visible through the same read stack, and `updateWhere` refuses a parent change — use `updateMany` or `move` |
| `treeClosure` | a closure table; needs `tree` as well (`treeclosure/needs-tree` without it) |
| `unique: [[...]]` | _(top-level)_ unique indexes, scope-folded when the resource is scoped; under softDelete or `immutable: { rectifiable: true }` the index is partial (`WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`) so a tombstone / superseded key does not lock the live set forever |
| `i18n: [...]` | _(top-level)_ a per-field translation sidecar (`ctx.i18n.resolve`; the field-level mark is `translatable()`) |
| `encrypted: [...]` | _(top-level)_ at-rest envelope encryption — a fresh data key per sealed field value, wrapped under an app key or your KMS. A read decrypts its whole batch or fails: one corrupted envelope or failed key unwrap fails the entire `list`, `find` or `search`, so a damaged row never passes as missing; `hazelnut rotate-key` isolates damaged rows one by one and names them |
| `sensitive: [...]` | _(top-level)_ audit diffs, event payloads, and matching `ctx.log` attrs apply `mask` (`****` / `***-1234`); HTTP drops the field on CRUD reads; MCP CRUD reads omit the key the same way (it never entered `columns`). A custom-op return that still names the field is masked to `[redacted]` on MCP and dropped on HTTP. Framework tracing carries no declared field values; deployment-owned spans are their own disclosure boundary |
| `i18nFallback: [...]` | _(top-level)_ the resolution order `ctx.i18n.resolve` walks after the requested locale — app-declared, never a framework default |
| `vector: {...}` | _(top-level)_ a pgvector embedding column, an HNSW index, and staleness shadows. Nearest-neighbour reads are the repo helper `semanticSearch` (you pass a pre-embedded query vector) — not HTTP QUERY, not `ctx.data` |
| `searchable: [...]` | _(top-level)_ native Postgres full-text search (tsvector + GIN). HTTP QUERY `search` only — MCP `list` has no `search` (it has `sort` instead) |
| `rollups: {...}` | _(top-level)_ maintained aggregates over child rows |
| `transitions: {...}` | _(top-level)_ a status state machine; `status` moves only along a declared transition |
| `idempotency` | accepted as a `features:{}` flag and inert. Arm the door with `idempotent: true` on a write op plus a client `Idempotency-Key` |

The full treatment of each, with the migration it implies, is in `docs/rundown.md`.

## The agent door

`POST /mcp` is served by a served app; `hazelnut mcp stdio|gateway` emits an entry for another
transport. The tools are CURATED: only operations a resource lists under `mcp:` become tools, each
owing a `describe`. Opening an HTTP route publishes no tool.

- `mcp.allowedOrigins` and `mcp.gate` are both REQUIRED on an app that serves tools — absence
  refuses at boot (`mcp/origin-declared`, `mcp/gate-declared`). `null` is the open door, declared.
- `gate` is read before the JSON-RPC body, so it answers for the whole door, handshake included.
- `tools/list` is narrowed per identity: a write tool the caller may not invoke is OMITTED, not
  refused. Absence in the list is not absence in the app.
- `confirm: true` adds a cooperative host hint; policy and rowPolicy enforce access. A curated `list` or
  `find` requires a `rowPolicy` or a deliberately public read (`mcp/read-protected`).
- One request object per call; a JSON-RPC batch is refused.

A versioned CRUD write carries its MCP `version` precondition. `NO_CAS` is framework-only: its
complete roster is cascade delete, set-null integrity sweep, expiry reaper, and a non-versioning
singleton replace — never an agent or application option.

## Scope and live updates

- `scope: true` stamps the scope resolver's value into `scope_key` on writes and conjoins it on
  reads. Resolve it from the authenticated actor, never a client header; a served app refuses a
  scoped resource without a resolver.
- Every `push.topics` key must also be in app or module `emits`. It exposes `GET /events/<topic>`
  only when its `observe(ctx, db)` policy allows the caller to learn that activity in their scope.
  An `invalidate` frame means refetch through the ordinary read door; it is not row authorization.
  `rows: { resource }` instead emits the current list projection and requires that resource's
  `http.list` door. Cookie auth can use EventSource; bearer auth needs a streaming fetch client
  that sends Authorization and parses SSE frames.

## Lifecycle jobs

- An expiry purge reaps each expired row through the ordinary remove path in its own savepoint. A
  blocked row stays expired and raises an alarm; other rows in that tick still purge, including
  their normal rollup, audit, and reverse-reference maintenance.

## Docs

- [docs/agent-door.md](docs/agent-door.md) — **How-to** — for a developer putting their app in front of an agent. One path, end to end: curate the tools, declare the posture, confirm what destroys, and know what the door does not promise. If you have never booted the framework, follow the [Quickstart](./QUICKSTART.md) first.
- [docs/cli/add.md](docs/cli/add.md) — **Reference** — for a developer growing an existing app. What `add` emits, what it registers for you, and what it deliberately leaves failing.
- [docs/cli/doctor.md](docs/cli/doctor.md) — **Reference** — for anyone whose app will not start, migrate, or serve. Checks the machine and the project's plumbing, and tells you the fix.
- [docs/cli/equality-cutover.md](docs/cli/equality-cutover.md) — **Reference** — for the operator making one key version canonical for encrypted equality lookups on unique fields.
- [docs/cli/install.md](docs/cli/install.md) — **Reference** — for anyone restoring the vendored framework tree into an app that was cloned without it.
- [docs/cli/launch.md](docs/cli/launch.md) — **Reference** — for whoever owns the production serve command. What each permission grant is derived from, what the verb refuses, and why it refuses instead of widening.
- [docs/cli/mcp.md](docs/cli/mcp.md) — **Reference** — for exposing your app's MCP surface over a transport other than the one the served app already mounts. Two doors, what each holds, and what each does not.
- [docs/cli/migrate.md](docs/cli/migrate.md) — **Reference** — for whoever changes the schema. Every subcommand, what it refuses, and what it does to your database.
- [docs/cli/new.md](docs/cli/new.md) — **Reference** — for scaffolding a fresh app. Every flag, what lands on disk, and how the framework gets pinned.
- [docs/cli/ops.md](docs/cli/ops.md) — **Reference** — for the operator pulling a production lever without a deploy.
- [docs/cli/redrive.md](docs/cli/redrive.md) — **Reference** — for the operator recovering dead-lettered outbox messages after fixing what made them fail.
- [docs/cli/relay.md](docs/cli/relay.md) — **Reference** — for anyone running the outbox drain as its own process. It drains the outbox and routes runtime alarms into your alarm sink.
- [docs/cli/rotate-key.md](docs/cli/rotate-key.md) — **Reference** — for the operator moving encrypted data keys onto a new master key version.
- [docs/cli/run-workflow.md](docs/cli/run-workflow.md) — **Reference** — for the operator starting or resuming a declared workflow from the command line.
- [docs/cli/unstick-workflow.md](docs/cli/unstick-workflow.md) — **Reference** — for the operator who knows a workflow runner is dead and does not want to wait for its step lease to lapse.
- [docs/cli/verify.md](docs/cli/verify.md) — **Reference** — for anyone gating a build. What the verb checks, what it does not, and how to read one finding.
- [docs/DEPLOY.md](docs/DEPLOY.md) — **How-to** — for whoever puts the app in production. One path, end to end: database, gated migration, container, probes, shutdown, observability.
- [docs/GLOSSARY.md](docs/GLOSSARY.md) — **Reference** — for anyone reading Hazelnut's documentation or its error messages. One concept, one name: these terms are used bare elsewhere, and this is where they are defined.
- [docs/QUICKSTART.md](docs/QUICKSTART.md) — **Tutorial** — for a developer who has never used Hazelnut. Follow it in order; every step is verifiable before you move on. Roughly fifteen minutes.
- [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) — Index
- [docs/refusals.md](docs/refusals.md) — **Reference** — for anyone reading a refusal line. Every refusal Hazelnut raises starts with an id; this page lists each one with the message it prints.
- [docs/rundown.md](docs/rundown.md) — **How-to** — for a developer building on Hazelnut. Task-oriented: find the concern, use the one supported way. If you have never booted the framework, follow the [Quickstart](./QUICKSTART.md) first — it is fifteen minutes and this page assumes it.
- [docs/VERSIONING.md](docs/VERSIONING.md) — **Reference** — for anyone pinning Hazelnut in a project. What a version number promises, how long a line is supported, and what an upgrade costs.
